PS5- FF Resonance (finished Phantom Blade Zero)Xbox- Warzone (MW4 integration hit at midnight)Switch 2- Zelda Ocarina of Time remakeSteam Deck- WoW Forever

Paused Phantom Blade Zero for the time being to play the Ocarina of Time Remake.

I gotta admit, the OoT Remake is amazing, big props to Nintendo, they did a great job with this remake, the game just oozes atmosphere and I love it a ton.

Greetings fellow video game enthusiasts. Let's just say I won't be going OOT much this weekend, if you know what i mean. (I actually have some commitments i can't get out of, including a boat trip to see seal pups, but I might take my Switch 2.) Happy gaming time everyone.

Mostly The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2. On PS5 I'll be mopping up trophies on Yakuza Kiwami 3 & Dark Ties. Haven't decided if I'm gonna go for the plat or not yet.

After three hack and slash games on the spin (Onimusha, Wolverine and PB0) I'll be going for something more sedate - Metal Gear Solid 4.

Indiana Jones and the Great Circle on PS5

I’m now near the end of Gizeh, and so far this game is 100% my style of game. This mixture of puzzles and versatile fighting is refreshing, and the (slapstick) humour couldn’t be better. The script is very entertaining, and Troy Baker does a tremendous job as Indy. The originality of all this is astonishing.

I am playing very slowly, doing almost all sidequests. Only the boxing clubs are a bit too difficult for me (playing in Hard, but maybe I’m not patient enough).

Earth defense force 5 and Onimusha 2 for me! Enjoying both. I would normally focus on one game but found EDF a little repetitive if you die and have to start long missions again, so needed Onimusha 2 to break things up and not kill my enthusiasm.

It's all about phantom blade zero this weekend as I actually have the time to dedicate myself to it. Fantastic and almost perfect game (personal opinion.) @GirlVersusGame glad you decided on GoW as it really is a brilliant game and I know you will enjoy the sequel more.

I decided to buy Fields of Mistria on PC and I’m so glad I did. It’s not a star dew clone and is much more accessible and has less constraints than star dew (stores open 24/7, save any time, characters show on the map etc) really really enjoying it. Perfect game to play before gta vi.

I took the advice of lots of you in the WAYP last weekend and started Phantom Blade Zero over Onimusha, as my final game to play and (hopefully) complete ahead of GTA VI. And all I can say is thanks for the advice - what a game, I absolutely love it. Alongside Galactic Racer as my more casual fallback I am having a blast. Enjoy the weekend all.

I'm really impatiently waiting for GTA VI now.

With PS Plus I hardly buy new games or find games on sale to be enticing. However, I did buy FF7: Rebirth and No Man's Sky but haven't actually installed them.

I plan on playing some PSVR2-titles including Walking Dead: Saint and Sinners (Tourist edition) and No Man's Sky. I have so many great PSVR2 adventures to catch up on, and if somehow my backlog from PSVR got ported (Star Wars Squadron, Astrobot, Iron Man, etc) I would have a lifetime supply.

I'm still at the end of Ball x Pit, but it sort of forces you to complete tracks with new characters prolonging its time to play. Funnily enough, one of the unlockable characters plays itself automatically and can be paired up with others. I had a novel time sending them off on the portal whilst working on my PC.

I also progressed a lot in KCD 2. I was on the hunt for killers and, unrelated, symbols belonging to a thieves' guild yesterday and today I might try and start Legacy of the Forge-dlc. I have been preparing to pass the Guild masters' test. Wish me luck😂

Just wanted to thank you both for recommending Another Zombie Zombie Survivors. At first I found it too difficult and gave up on it, but because of your positive thoughts on it, I decided to give it another try, figured out how to upgrade my abilities and characters and ended up having a blast! I got the platinum just a few days ago.

I also just bought Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game and I'm enjoying it so far, likely mostly because I'm a big fan of the show.

On the recommendation of @girlversusgame I started and finished Midnight Walk. Superb experience in terms of atmosphere and storytelling, albeit not a tier 1 game - if that makes sense

I have then been on a Game Trial mission to discover some possible future purchases

Eriksholm was a stand-out for me. A very relaxing stealth game with an incredible isometric world.

Absolutely loved Pragmata too. The hacking mechanic was great fun.

Stellar Blade visually is pretty cool but maybe too soulslike for my taste

Finally, I finally tried Witcher 3. Already hooked on the story but I can tell i may feel a little overwhelmed

Next up will be Resident Evil Requiem. Keen.

@naruball glad to help spend your cash 🤣. I've pre ordered warhammer survivors which is out next week. Looks awesome.

I usually like to say I’m playing some obscure game from the PS1 or PS2 days to look cooler than I actually am…..

But no, I’m playing Ocarina of Time remake today.

Feeling spoiled with great games of late 🙂

The Wolf Among US - Finished and platinumed. Such a great game this, I love it. Telltale at some its best imo. Even having played it twice before I got emotionally invested which is what makes it so good, on top of that its a good story too. Really looking forward to TWAU 2 🙂

Phantom Blade 0 - This is also really, really good. Not played that much yet, maybe 12 hours or so, but having a blast. My son also really likes it. He plays on hard, as he is a big fan of soulslikes (which this isnt, really), and gets a good challenge whereas I´m playing on easy (tired parent/old man mode, much appriceated) which is so far not difficult at all but a lot less time consuming I guess. The fighting and the flow of it and the animations is just on another level. The story is a bit hard to follow, but the cutscenes are well made. Its also a very good looking game with some great artistic designs. Its a game that both looks and makes you feel really cool. Hoping to finish and platinum this one before GTA 6 🙂

@GirlVersusGame yeah, 7 😄. I’m regularly playing: SIlver Pines (evenings) Cocoon (evenings) Inscryption (evenings)

Pony Island (pc, just finished) Order of the Sinking Star (great pick-up-and-play puzzler with a million different mechanics) Final Fantasy Resonance (the main game at the moment) Noita The Hex (just started) GT7 (but I’ve played it every week for 4 years with VR)

Oh, and I just got Still Wakes The Deep but I haven’t started it yet. Midnight Walk is on my wishlist too

I’m not sure if I’ve recommended The Vanishing of Ethan Carter, I noticed it on my Steam list and downloaded it again. It’s a beautiful walking simulator from about 2014 and has some gorgeous music in it (Mikolai Stroinski)

I think you’ll love Zelda, it’s got a horse in it😄. The only reason I’m not getting Zelda is because I just didn’t think the Switch 2 was a big enough upgrade over the Switch. Maybe on the Switch 3

Just started Zero Parades for Dead Spies. I’m only an hour in but it is a very trippy game which reminds me a lot of old text driven point and click adventure games like Police Quest (I know it’s a spiritual successor to Disco Elysium).

I’m also playing Phantom Blade Zero (this one side boss is beating me so bad I might come back to him later once I’m stronger), GT7, Mewgenics and Helldivers 2.

Me and my wife are taking turns having play sessions on Ocarina of time (we both loved the N64 original), loving it all over again.

I finally bought the wolf among us remastered when I got the correct discount showing so that's an option to play if the Mrs plays ocarina or in handheld mode

Still playing Dragon Quest: Echoes of an elusive age, which will keep me busy for a while. I’ve also replaying some Stardew Valley for some light fun.

Chained echoes for the win and some Fallout 4 for seconds

@Blauwe_Chimay I’ve been looking to get this myself, but hear there can be quite a lot of crashes, and this puts me off. Have you experienced any, and do you know if you lose a lot of progress?

Legacy of Kain: Blood Omen, Rayman Legends and maybe Sea of Thieves.

Road Rash 30th anniversary edition on the Xbox Ally X. Upgraded version of the brilliant 3do game. Very fun. Can they do the 3do version of Need for Speed next please.

Having now wrapped up the spooky season games I was playing in now gonna get back to GoW Ragnorok and hopefully I will click with not a bit more than when I dropped it.... Realised time is fast running out to get to the games I hoped to compete in 2026!Also gonna start up Agent Intercept for something a bit more arcadey.Have a good weekend whatever you're up to people.

Zelda Ocarina of Time(S2) Playing this again for the first time in nearly 30 years has brought back fond memories. This remake looks absolutely gorgeous, and is everything I wanted it to be. I still think Nintendo missed a trick by not having a gold case and cartridge, but at least I got the foil cover. Currently exploring Kakariko village. Phantom Blade Zero(PS5) Have just left the Crimson Desert and am now in the village of Lu. Didn’t quite realise going into this game how much of a 3D metroidvania it is as well! Star Wars Galactic Racer(PS5) Act 3 is hard! You don’t get as many league tokens, so it’s much easier to get knocked out before you even reach Kestar Bool.

I am doing the collectible run in Alan Wake II before going to the final acts. I will plat this game, and them do the DLCs. Great game!!

I will continue Trails in The Sky 2nd Chapter. Investigating another town, meeting dear friends again... This game knows how to hit the feels.

And, doing the last sidequests and collectibles in God of War: Sons of Sparta. They packed a lot more than I expected in this metroidvania game. But I will hunt the platinum there too!!

gonna try absolum thanks to @playstation1995

Castlevania with new Xbox nano controller which i only got to work on tablet and not pc like it says on box.

I'm about 44hrs into FF Resonance I might actually Platinum this one!

More Star Wars Galactic Racer, determined to get through Act 2 this weekend, that last eliminator before the final race is tough!Also some Drift Out on the Evercade.

@nomither6 go for it absolum is so amazing a beat em up roguelike.and the gameplay and the graphics. Soundtrack and boss fights are amazing.its the best rogue like games I ever play Word up son

Back in 2020 a little game called Othercide released. I pre-ordered the game and earned every Achievement in it. At the beginning of this year, I moved to predominantly playing on my Pro (which I bought in January), and I have spent a fair bit of money rebuying games that I first bought on Xbox for PlayStation instead. Othercide is one of those games, and last night I unlocked the Platinum for it. It is such a good strategy game, and I highly recommend it.

With Othercide beaten, just before midnight last night I began playing Phantom Blade Zero, and that will be the game I next play to completion. I'm liking what little I have played of it so far, and it looks stunning on the Pro...

Finished Trails in The Sky 2nd chapter and Resonance A Plague Tale Legacy this week so I'm either going to start Metro 2033 or finally start The Witcher 3 Remastered. Trails is now one of my favourite series and i only discovered it in September absolutely loved every minute of 1st and 2nd chapter remakes.

GT7 Weekly Challenges and Zelda OOT Remake.

Crimson Desert on PC - lookin mighty fine with a 5090. I could cry 😭. Gotta get to the end game so I can play that awesome-looking DLC. This is absolutely my GOTY by a long shot, with such a fantastically detailed natural world.

I've also been playing Silent Hill Townfall which has an incredibly grim and bleak vibe. Promising so far but we'll see how the story goes.

The (not so) wildcard that I've picked up again is Starfield which is pretty dull compared to the other Bethesda titles, yet for some reason I've come back to it many times for it's space sim comfort. Definitely a 6/10 game but also somehow addictive in its own way.

I’m still working through - and loving - Onimusha and Resident Evil 4 Remake. But I finally picked up Phantom Blade Zero last night. Feels great so far. It might take over the weekend. We’ll see.

Witcher 3 and phantom blade zero afterwards 😁

Playing as a dual-wielding tech expert nomad in Cyberpunk 2077 and as the first human spectre and all-round N7 badass (Femshep) in Mass Effect.

@Carnage Mewgenics is such a good time and the soundtrack is fantastic. Have you tried Disco Elysium or did you jump to Zero Parades? The former was my first point and click game, my last one was Discworld on Playstation One (it's really hard) Zero Parades I haven't started yet, I'm following the original developers games too.

@DrVenture69 I still need to finish your Silent Hill 3 diary, I spent most of the week outside running around with animals but I'm curious to see where things go next. Somewhere horrible I'm sure. I lost track with all of the other feedback, replied to the wrong person, deleted it and lost the posts. I could never play three games in one evening, I definitely wouldn't be allowed. I need to see what Pony Island is (checks) okay that's not what I was expecting. I thought it was more like Horse Tales or Barbie Horse Trails. I'm looking forward to hearing about your Still Wakes The Deep experience, it won't take long to get through and like The Midnight Walk you won't forget it. I'll make sure to add Ethan Carter, I did play Breath of The Wild and mainly went with Nintendo for AnimalCrossing. I've tried Mario Sunshine too and not much else. Do you ever sleep?

@Northern_munkey Tuesday is going to be so good, I've done a good job at not looking at the other developer videos. God of War is one of those 'I should have tried this ages ago' kind of games, when I play a lot of janky weird games I sometimes forget that Triple-A even exists. Everything is so well made, it feels like I'm in one of my art-books. Instead of just looking at concept art and thinking 'it kind of looks like that', the interactions are so human too. It's like Kratos is giving me real life lessons. 'we do what we must to survive. Not because we are animals, not because we are revenge-driven, but because we must', my Dad said something similar, he was right too and he had an axe.

@old_gamer74 Oh brilliant, it definitely does some really unique and special things. For such a short playthrough there's nothing to lose but a couple of hours. My best advice for The Witcher 3 is to stick with it, I was overwhelmed and lost with the story too and the more I played the more sense it made. Combat gets easier and flows better the more geared you become, if you run into trouble with Gwent buy spy cards from vendors and play as the Northern Realms. They make Gwent easier and Quen (shield) will make combat easier until you get your rotations down. Parry humans, dodge monsters, I didn't roll much it drains stamina. The bestiary was one of my biggest boons, it explains how to defeat the various enemies. You'll earn more by selling weapons to blacksmiths, armor to armorer. Sometimes dismantle is better than selling, example shells into pearls, it's a higher markup. Also get the DLC if you haven't already, it's some of the best DLCs of any game.

@naruball I experienced the same thing with the game. The first couple of times I played I kept getting overrun by zombies and struggled to clear even one map. After a couple of runs I started to build the first class and quickly saw a difference. I think my favorite feature is that while you can upgrade stats for the whole character roster, you can upgrade each character solo too and they get really strong. My favorite combination was the Mercenary, Medic and Shotgun man. It gets so satisfying when endless mode is unlocked and the confidence is there to just go for it. I think my longest run was three-hours, I had a podcast playing and they were doing all of the heavy lifting.

@DennisReynolds Do you still have to look after all of those animals while they are away or are the animals work as in you go from your home to a farm or animal sanctuary and then that's work?

@ApostateMage I might try Mass Effect after God of War and Grand Theft Auto Six, it would be the trilogy (more than likely) would you say there is a good balance of action/traversal when compared to dialogue/story? my biggest concern is the possibility of being buried under so much dialogue and not being able to keep up.

@EfYI I finished Ballxpit this week and the character you mean is the same one I talked about on chitchat a couple of days ago, it's basically automatic mode. I let that guy do his thing for hours while I read books and played other games. It's cheating but the developers put him in there for a reason. There are some interesting unlocks at the end of the game, they make playing the game forever possible.

Picked up Kena on sale for $15.99. Good deal. Would’ve been an even better deal if I’d played it when it was available via PS+. Anyway, starting it today. Wish me fun!

I’m playing Pragmata and COD MW4 MP. Pragmata is excellent and has an interesting twist to it with the hacking aspect of it. Capcom definitely came up with a solid, interesting and fun gameplay concept there. As for COD MW4, say what you will about the series, this year’s offering is a strong one. The campaign is one of the series best and the MP is excellent as well. The adherence to military simulation instead of goofy skins is nice as is the fact that any XP tokens only get used in real time. Definitely a plus there. Anyways, I hope everyone enjoys their gaming this weekend and as always, no rage quitting!

I'm trying to finish what I started and complete the 007 game, but I'm very tempted to just jump into Zelda ...and I'm ready for, you know...

Whatever you are playing, I hope you and yours have a great time.

@GirlVersusGame I'd say that there is far more dialogue than action in the first game, a fair mix in ME2 whilst the third game is far more action and combat orientated. I actually dislike ME3 a lot because there's a lot of auto dialogue (Shepard speaks without player input) and there a far fewer dialogue choices compared to the first two games. I feel that Shepard turns into a moron throughout ME3.

@DETfaninATL As for COD MW4, say what you will about the series, this year’s offering is a strong one.

Edit: I just realized I haven't spent any XP yet, I missed a whole skill menu. It's because I'd been using silver to buy upgrades and thought he was automatically levelling. No wonder I was being bounced around so much even with upgrades.

@ApostateMage I think I'll try the first one and see where it goes from there, I'm not sure how I feel about auto dialogue. Especially in a game like that, it sounds like it would defeat the whole purpose of player choice. It would be mostly just to play a part of history, that's how I view a lot of big franchises and lately everyone is talking about Bioware. I played the Dragon Age set on PS3, Origins, Two and the DLCs. Inquisition was the other I finished, Veilguard I haven't gotten to yet. There are too many games and not enough hours, unless you have some cyberware for sleep. Judge Dredd sleeps for ten-minutes each day, I think DrVenture69 does too.

Not much of a trophy Hunter but it's doable. It's just a big grind. Did the weapondives first. This will help you a lot.

I have The Midnight Walk installed but I plan this and RE:R to play in January. January is my horror gaming month.

Are you going to play Warhammer Survivors or Raccoin on Tuesday?

I'm playing Queens Domain. It's kicking my arse. I'm having fun. I'm also going to try ng+ in valhalla.

No crashes for me. Sometimes there is an occasional fps drop when there are too many drones (a weapon type) on screen. Only happened 3 or 4 times. I had over 60 drones on screen + 200 enemies.

When you die during a dive, you gain the minerals to upgrade your skills. Also all the equipment you find isn't lost.

I recommend this game if you love other Survivors games.

@GirlVersusGame it’s more of a rotation thing, a couple of evenings of Silver Pines, a couple of evenings of Cocoon. I try to be good and stop at 9:00pm. But after GTA6 comes out, there might only be one game. I was hoping for a 60fps performance mode, but I’ll probably get it anyway. I want to explore every centimetre of that map.

Yeah, pony island was the best kind of weird. 10% a rudimentary pony jumping game, 90% meta game trying to hack into the game in order to escape from it. Inscryption is similar, but its got a really good card game instead of ponies

@Blauwe_Chimay Thanks muchly, downloading it now.

@Blauwe_Chimay I don't know where I'll be geographically on Tuesday but the moment that game goes live I'm jumping in. My plan is to play Warhammer in the morning/afternoon and try Raccoin in the evening/night. The funny thing about Raccoin is I only watched a trailer, I don't really know what's involved just that it looks like a lot of fun, is soaked in dopamine and I'm all for supporting Indies. You might know this already but there's a new class/map coming for Deep Rock Galactic Survivor, sometime this month as a paid DLC, I believe they are melee and the map is Sand something.

@4fold I've had no crashes and I know it's been running for hours without a break, a lot of enemies can be on screen like Blue Chimay said, I had not even a stutter so far. I'll add to what they said about the equipment, it can be sold too and you can buy extra materials/minerals needed for those same permanent upgrades. I'd put off playing it for a while because I thought that by not playing the non-survivors Deep Rock Galactic game I'd be missing out on some of the lore/and felt like I'd arrived late to the party. It didn't matter, it's really easy to pick up and play, but hard to put down. I've played a bunch of the survivors genre now and I'd say it's more mature and requires more thinking than most other survivors. Not mature as in graphic, it feels like a Dad game in the best way possible. It's gruffer, rougher and tougher, you'll feel like you worked a day down the mines and might even grow a beard. I did die a lot at the start but each time came away wanting to try again and see what the other classes did/how different weapons worked and so on.

@DrVenture69 That makes more sense, I thought you were playing three each evening. Even two for me is a lot, I usually go one for console and the other is portable. That's why survivors have been such a great genre, they are easy to pick up and put down and I can play them at all kinds of events and still seem to be paying attention. I've had to move this evenings plans around for more gaming, I didn't count on God of War being this good or that I could throw an axe. Throwing things in games is one of my favorite mechanics, I got through Hitman by using only fire extinguishers. They are really heavy and knock people right out, this axe is too but it comes right back. It travels a lot further too, I wish I'd had it in Silent Hill 2.

Its got to the point where I don't want to start anything too big before GTA VI so I'm going to be playing Mafia The Old Country through PS Plus. So far I've been enjoying it. Simple gameplay that works as well as it needs to with great performances during the story segments.

Still need to finish up Fatal Frame 2 Remake. I think I'm close to finishing it and I have to say I've really enjoyed this one. A top tier horror game that I'll definitely replay in the future!

I'll still be casually chipping away at Mina The Hollower as well. I'm really bad at it 😅

Got the 'Lack of a Switch 2 and Ocarina of Time' Blues™️

Finished Vampire Survivors on Switch this morning, which is my fourth completion. Reckon I should put it down now and try Vampire Crawlers 😅

Undecided on Dishonored, absolutely love it but get that feeling it isn't the right time.

Bloodborne for the first time playthrough..about 5 hours in and loving it.

@DrVenture69 apologies, I've only just noticed your Silver Pines rec, it definitely looks right up my strasse! Thank you sir

@AgentCooper , no worries😄. It’s not super Twin Peaks adjacent, but the story and voice acting are really good. Basically a detective trying to solve a murder in an almost abandoned town due to a “weather event”, but you’re constantly finding items to unlock other areas. The first couple of bosses can take a few goes but you get better weapons after that.

@GirlVersusGame The GoW axe would be awesome in silent hill 2, except for P-Head, I can hear the clang as it bounces off him😄

@DrVenture69 Oh right I completely forgot about what his head was made of, I'd probably deafen myself in the process. I feel like it might be a great way to fight him, banging the pipe off his head so he's stunned as you kick him in the shins or something. Sort of like Mars Attacks where they used 'Indian Love Call' by Slim Whitman to defeat the martians with the yodeling over loudspeakers.

@AgentCooper Congrats on number four, I've hundreds of hours in and still haven't beaten death. Everyone says 'oh kat just use freeze', it doesn't work he grinds on me with his scythe every time. That said I wasn't even aware of the game having an ending. I keep playing the same maps with the same characters and now Poncle are about to bless us again this Tuesday, I hope it goes well for them I'd love to see them do more tie-in/collaborations and this one has such big DLC possibilities, hopefully that's what happens.

Finishing my second 100% play through with End of Abyss. My favourite game of the year for me. Should have the Platinum Trophy tomorrow. And I start to explore Hyrule with young Link and see what all the fuss is about.

Yeah I never played one of earlier versions, since I was a PC gamer only for a long time.

On PS5 I´ll be playing RE Requiem - it is indeed fantastic game and Leon is a boss character. I purchased Little Nightmares 2 for my steamdeck to continue my spooky gaming season but I´ll start this one after I finish Requiem first as I really suck at playing multiple games at once...

In TV I´ll be watching some PL football with little bits of NHL/NBA hopefully. I know it´s only beginning of November, but already looking foward to Christmas holidays to finally not think about work and simply have more time for gaming and relax

Anyway, have a great weekend and enjoy games you all playing. Cheers everyone

@GirlVersusGame Once you have the yellow sign, go for the Infinite Corridor and Crimson Shroud, that sorts old skull face right out. I've only 100% everything on xbox, but have given up keeping up with Poncle's workrate. I'll support the hell out of them wherever they release games though. I have 100s of combined hours at this point and probably could play it forever. Are you going to be playing Warhammer Survivors?

@AgentCooper I'm not sure what the yellow sign is or the infinite corridor or the crimson shroud. Thank you I wrote it all down for when I'm feeling more focused on actual completion. My progress at the moment is the following:

Collection 136 of 205Bestiary 144 of 217Unlocks 151 of 217Secrets 10 of 26

Maps I've run: Mad Forest, Inlaid Library, Dairy Plant, Gallo Tower, Cappelle Magna, Il Molise, and the others I'm not sure if I've even tried before because I always end up running the same maps.

I've mostly been using Clerici, Dommario, Poe, Mortaccio, O'Sole and recently tried Amrojoe after finding that Kinderegg (icon) looking power where furniture flies everywhere. Chula-Reh was recent too. There are seven whole rows of characters not unlocked and I've just been waiting until I randomly find the unlock condition by playing. I've been treating it as one big forever game and thought that even by a fluke I'd have beaten death by now. I tend to just pick one map then run it for hours while I read or do other things.

As for Warhammer Survivors I'll be on there the moment it goes live and will try to post some feedback after the first couple of hours. I'm not sure about the Warhammer part, the franchise is massive and for me largely unknown but it looks like a really good game.

Welcome back to Conformity Gate. With Stranger Things Day sending us all back to the Upside Down today, Sony has the headphones to pair with that world-saving Walkman. The brand has just announced a Stranger Things edition of the new MDR-3R wired headphones, now available with bold red cushions (and a black set included in the box). The $79 / £59 Stranger Things variant bumps up the price of the new release a little (the standard model starts at $59 / £49) but maintains a style fit for Hawkins.

The Sony MDR-3R headphones are being described as "Newtro" by the brand, combining more modern audio handling (and a USB-C connection) with the instantly recognizable retro aesthetic. Sony has faithfully reconstructed the MDR-3 design, with that skinny band, chunky silver driver plate, and simple design. If we ever needed another reason to start running up that hill, this is it.

The new Sony MDR-3Rs are still waiting to go live on the brand's own site, though notifications are available if you want to be one of the first in the line. It's worth noting that the red-cushion Stranger Things version is a limited edition, so keep that refresh button warm.

So what does the Stranger Things edition bring to its higher price tag? It's a subtle one. The blue / orange cushion color options of the standard model are replaced with a deep Upside Down red and black pairing with a Stranger Things logo stamped at the top of the headband.

If you're going for the full '80s aesthetic, you'd be better off with the orange base option, saving yourself some cash in the process. If you're going like-for-like with Max herself, you'll need the limited edition to get access to those black pads.

The headphones themselves are constructed from a lightweight aluminum and stainless steel, powered by that USB-C connection for a charge-free experience, and still feature an inline remote with an integrated microphone for media control and calls.

Sony says it's kept the MDR-3R sound profile as close to the original as possible, while still elevating sound with some more modern features. That open-back design is still going to give your music plenty more breathing space, but the brand has extended both lower and upper ranges for a more dynamic quality.

While the absence of that ninth episode still continues to hurt, at least we've got some tunes to see us through. Plus, with Maya Hawke joining the Magic: The Gathering movie there's still plenty from the series stars in the works.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a remake masterpiece, but takes one leap too far

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I'm on a roll as I enter Dodongo's Cavern, the fiery labyrinth and second dungeon in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. Despite plenty of tweaks and changes, muscle memory of my previous playthroughs has kept me on task – adult wallet acquired, deku nuts on lock, Hylian Shield strapped on my back. Then, I walk forward a few steps towards ledges above flaming pools of lava and immediately faceplant, my poor little elfin boy immediately set aflame. Yes, Navi, I need some hearts.

Perhaps the biggest gameplay change in Ocarina of Time remake compared to the Nintendo 64 original is swapping the auto-jump to a manual button press. Previously, running toward an edge would have the green-garbed Link always jump from the furthest point possible. Now, I have to press a button to do it myself. Great. And why don't I rock up to my local pizza place to bake my own pie next time I order, too? While I see Super Mario 64 challenge runs completing that game without jumping at all, I've been doomed to tap the jump-button in the Zelda equivalent endlessly.

I'm exaggerating, but only a bit. There are actually loads of times in which the manual control of Link's hops, and how reactive all his moves are in a world that feels utterly teeming with life, helps this remake buzz with a new energy. Small layout changes to early areas add a smidge more naturalistic verticality to some zones, while scampering through towns and mantling ledges simply makes navigation of the overworld much more swish.

Still, it's in the more traditional Zelda dungeon exploration and challenges that I stumble. I'm so used to routing my way through these dangerous areas by pointing myself in the right direction and chaining together auto-jumps that I find myself forgetting or mistiming the input to go early or roll by mistake and end up going splat. This is very embarrassing to admit as a big platformer fan who usually wastes no time click-clacking the stick to do side somersaults up forbidden pathways. Something about having to press the jump button in Ocarina of Time is vexing me. And I'm far from the only one.

In part, it's because I have played these games before. These jumps are deeply familiar to me, designed without a manual jump button at all, only to now have the need foisted upon them. It's not like Elden Ring where the addition of a more natural jump compared to Dark Souls was incorporated into its level design approach from the ground-up.

While the position of, say, the pond with the platforms in Kokiri Village may have been adjusted, the sequence is the same as the original. Except, now, you have to press another button the whole time while doing it rather than thinking only about steering.

I'm being picky, and a bit of a grumbler – I do agree with Anna's 5-star Ocarina of Time remake review. This is an exceptional overhaul. But, it's not as if the concept of a jump-button was completely alien to the N64 development team – the original game was intentionally designed not to need a jump button. It's not like they just forgot to include it.

Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week

In fact, I'd say more isn't always better – like a sloppy, delicious-looking burger with too many toppings to get your jaw around. For me, some of the joy of revisiting classic Zelda is the simplicity of control that allows depth elsewhere. It's not as if auto-jumping was an N64 limitation, the traversal mechanic having remained in the series all the way through to Breath of the Wild.

Many of the best Zelda games, as a result, make fantastic use of auto-jump without the need for manual jump at all – Wind Waker, Twilight Princess, all the rest. In Breath of the Wild it made sense with the design shift to the open world, freeform focused exploration, away from tight dungeon design. Ocarina of Time remake isn't so different that this fundamental control choice suddenly needs an overhaul.

I'm not fuming it's here, but I'm a bit baffled at the dedication to manual jump. If you're going to add it in, why not keep auto-jump as a toggle or additional option? After all, the Ocarina of Time remake dev team explicitly kept the classic jump-attack and rolling options alongside their modern control versions. Granted, some reworked sections now require manual jumping – climbing up a bit of wall into the Hyrule Castle gardens, for example, which I quite like – but why does that mean I also can't auto-jump when I run at an edge?

Largely, Ocarina of Time remake is a more well-considered overhaul than I had first feared. Over the last few years, I've been finding remakes broadly very hit and miss. Loads of small tweaks feel dialled in to perfection, from the exact amount of luscious detail to enemy animations making combat feel more reactive – all while respecting much of the core design that made Ocarina of Time such a classic. But, when I'm tumbling into the lava because I forgot that not all original design concepts are quite so revered as others at the altar of strapping on more game mechanics, well, it burns a little.

Time marches on. Check out our upcoming Switch 2 releases for more adventures on the horizon!

Much of the focus has been on Zelda: Ocarina of Time this week, but in case you missed it, Call of Duty: Warzone is now available to download for the Switch 2.

This is a free-to-play battle royale experience, where you can squad up and drop in. It's a separate mode from the Modern Warfare 4 single-player, multiplayer and DMZ mode.

It can be downloaded via the eShop and requires an Activision account to play. On our end, our total file size is now 122GB.

Alongside this is the release of Season 1 for Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone. In the MW4 multiplayer, this seasonal update comes loaded with additional multiplayer maps (Backstab, Canyon, Shoot House and more), modes, events, and rewards across both the game's multiplayer and DMZ. The STJV union says Microsoft imposed hiring freezes at Arkane that resulted in delays and additional expenses, which it then cited as reasons for shutting it down.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

"After freezing hiring for 19 months, which artificially caused delays and additional cost, Microsoft now uses those same delays and additional costs as a reason to close down the studio."

France's Syndicat des Travailleureuses du Jeu Vidéo (STJV) union has accused Microsoft of sabotaging work on Marvel's Blade and then using the inevitable results to justify Arkane's closure.

The union said development of Blade "is going fine," and that the game is on par with Arkane's previous body of work, which includes the Dishonored series, Prey, Deathloop, and the sadly overlooked Dark Messiah of Might and Magic. Despite that, "workers have to face the harsh reality: our studio might get closed because, and only because, Microsoft decided to, even if that means sabotaging the game it funded."

"Microsoft chose to justify the closure on economic reasons," the union wrote. "But Microsoft is actually why those economic reasons even exist. Because after freezing hiring for 19 months, which artificially caused delays and additional cost, Microsoft now uses those same delays and additional costs as a reason to close down the studio."

Closing Arkane would defy "financial logic," the union claimed, as it would likely cost more money than just allowing it to finish Blade—and furthermore, it added, Arkane is profitable—"just not profitable enough for Microsoft."

"Microsoft is responsible for the situation Arkane is in today. Microsoft is responsible for the situation the workers are in today," the union said. "So Microsoft has to take full responsibility here and act accordingly."

While its "dearest wish" is to see Arkane "live on," STJV said the studio's future has to go beyond just completing Blade. And if that's not feasible and Arkane must close, it falls to Microsoft—"the company who decided that Arkane has to shut down"—to take care of the hundreds of lives it has thrown into turmoil. Given Microsoft's essentially limitless resources, the union believes the company has a moral obligation to go beyond the bare minimum required by law: "We will not allow the lives of Arkane Studios' workers to be destroyed without the company paying a fair price."

The union is not aiming low with its demands. First, "to give employees control over the decisions that shape their future" while acquisition negotiations are underway:

From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews

Should Arkane ultimately be closed, it demands Microsoft "funds commensurate with Microsoft’s status as a corporation" to ensure employees are properly compensated:

Those are big asks, but the union isn't wrong about the resources Microsoft has at its disposal: Microsoft's net income for the first quarter of FY27 was $36.6 billion. Xbox is a small contributor to that total, but it is a part of Microsoft, and that makes it Microsoft's issue to deal with.

For now, the fate of Arkane remains unresolved: The studio fell victim to the most recent round of cuts at Xbox, but a recent report indicated that it might yet find a home with a new owner. I've reached out to Xbox for comment on the STJV union's demands and will update if I receive a reply.

Andy has been gaming on PCs from the very beginning, starting as a youngster with text adventures and primitive action games on a cassette-based TRS80. From there he graduated to the glory days of Sierra Online adventures and Microprose sims, ran a local BBS, learned how to build PCs, and developed a longstanding love of RPGs, immersive sims, and shooters. He began writing videogame news in 2007 for The Escapist and somehow managed to avoid getting fired until 2014, when he joined the storied ranks of PC Gamer. He covers all aspects of the industry, from new game announcements and patch notes to legal disputes, Twitch beefs, esports, and Henry Cavill. Lots of Henry Cavill.

On the road to Avengers: Doomsday, Black Panther: Wakanda Forever remains Marvel's best passing of the torch

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Shuri was never supposed to be the Black Panther. In 2020, Chadwick Boseman, who portrayed T'Challa with so much regal gravitas, died at the age of 43. In the terrible aftermath, Black Panther: Wakanda Forever was released – a beautiful entry in the MCU that functions both as a deeply loving tribute to Boseman and an emotional passing of the torch to Letitia Wright's Shuri.

It's this context that makes Black Panther: Wakanda Forever such an extraordinary accomplishment. Not only is it a genuinely thrilling chapter in the MCU, but it also pulls off the tricky task of handing over the mantle in a way that feels respectful and natural to the characters involved, while honoring the real Boseman. It doesn't shy away from this reality, instead choosing to tell a story that focuses heavily on Shuri's raw grief and her complicated journey to stepping up as her nation's protector.

Now, Shuri is set to return in Avengers: Doomsday, standing alongside other Marvel titans like Chris Hemsworth's Thor and the original X-Men. I just hope that, among the stacked cast, Shuri gets her chance to shine – because she's earned it.

Wakanda Forever begins with T'Challa dying from a mystery illness. Despite her super-genius intellect, Shuri is powerless against this invisible enemy and unable to synthesize a new heart-shaped herb, and so T'Challa dies. Shuri, who idolized her big brother, is devastated – and, after a time-skip of a year, she is still struggling with her all-encompassing grief, which is making her as angry as she is heartbroken.

Welcome to Road to Doomsday, GamesRadar+'s weekly MCU rewatch series. Over 15 weeks, we'll be revisiting each Marvel movie and TV show on Disney's list of essential movies to watch ahead of Avengers: Doomsday, sharing our thoughts upon rewatching and deciphering what we can learn about the next Marvel mega-event from each entry. Why not relive some MCU highlights and watch along with us?

It's this raw emotion that makes Shuri's journey to becoming a fully fledged hero so compelling. Shuri, very understandably, does not want to become the Black Panther. It doesn't even cross her mind. Instead, she has the incredibly human reaction of simply wanting to grieve. But in the Marvel universe, nobody has any breathing space for long, and the arrival of Namor and the threat of CIA intervention over Vibranium pushes Shuri back into the fray. It's when the situation spirals out of control, and Namor kills her mother, Queen Ramonda, that Shuri finally returns to attempting to reconstruct the heart-shaped herb.

As a showdown with Killmonger in the Ancestral Plane demonstrates, though, Shuri is not solely motivated by an altruistic desire to be a hero: she wants revenge. Her anger and pain at the loss of T'Challa have been exacerbated by the murder of her mother, resulting in a furious grief that threatens to plunge Wakanda into an endless war with its underwater neighbours. It's a natural breaking point in her struggle to deal with so much loss, and sets Shuri's arc apart from the rise to greatness of other MCU heroes in its messy, intense vulnerability and pain.

Ultimately, though, Shuri, movingly encouraged by the spirit of Ramonda, chooses peace by sparing Namor's life and putting an end to the fighting between Wakanda and Talokan. This triumphant finish clears the way, allowing Shuri to finally process her grief – and even meet her nephew, T'Challa II. Her story in the film ends with a quiet moment on the beach, burning her mourning clothes, letting go of the painful past in order to face a more hopeful future.

Shuri's journey is not easy, and it's not one she even wanted – mirroring the awful real-life circumstances that led to the storyline. In this anguish is a beautiful evolution, powered by a standout performance from Wright, that brings Shuri from the fun, kid sister sidekick to the Black Panther herself. This passing of the torch is so effective because it truly means something, both within the MCU and in real life, and it gifts Shuri with boundless potential.

It was announced at SDCC that Shuri will soon be passing on the mantle herself, this time to T'Challa II. The Long Walk star David Jonsson will play the character, though how it will all work out is unclear at the moment, since Jonsson is much older than the young T'Challa II at the end of Wakanda Forever. ("In this next film, he grows up, comes of age, and we had to find an incredible actor," director Ryan Coogler shared on stage.)

This passing of the torch is so effective because it truly means something

Hopefully, then, Shuri gets her chance to shine in Avengers: Doomsday before surrendering the mantle. This is her first opportunity to truly spread her wings as the Black Panther after Wakanda Forever, and, with such a stacked cast, there's every risk Shuri might fall by the wayside – which would be a huge mistake, after how far she has come. She can be glimpsed in the trailers so far, though sadly not for very long.

Before Avengers: Doomsday, Spider-Man: No Way Home proved the best Marvel event movies put character first

But Wright may have already inadvertently let slip that she's part of the Avengers: Secret Wars cast, which would mean we have one more chance after Doomsday to see her in all her power before Jonsson takes over in Black Panther 3. What might happen in Secret Wars heavily depends on Doomsday, of course, but this duo of blockbuster event films offers the perfect chance to bring Shuri's MCU story to a meaningful close, paying off the emotional set-up of Wakanda Forever.

Shuri was never supposed to be the Black Panther, but she has more than proved how capable she is of being Wakanda's protector – and I hope Doomsday gives her the chance to truly show it.

Black Panther: Wakanda Forever is available to stream now on Disney Plus, ahead of the release of Avengers: Doomsday on December 18.

#4137. Talking Point: What Are You Playing This Weekend? (November 7-8)

Just two more weekends to get stuck into the games you're likely to abandon come November 19th.

It's been a fairly chill week for new releases with ZERO PARADES: Director's Cut the only notable launch (at least in my opinion). Hopefully something from our Deep Discounts sales roundup, or Xbox's Free Play Days titles are worth a shot.

Alrighty then, let's get into it. Here's what we're playing on Xbox this weekend:

I think I'm in need of a nice, feel good weekend of gaming. I'd like to play stuff that leaves me feeling all warm and fuzzy. It's appropriate timing, really, considering just how quickly it's getting dark now that the clocks have changed here in the UK.

Top of the agenda is starting The Wolf Among Us Remastered. I claimed the original version with Games with Gold, yet I've still not managed to boot it. Somehow, I've managed to avoid all spoilers in the thirteen year stretch. All I know is there's a pig called Colin or something. Anyway, I'm very excited to finally play it, as I've only ever heard good things about it.

Another game I'd like to experience for the first time is It Takes Two. My lady love and I are looking for our next co-op adventure after completing Split Fiction, so what better choice than Hazelight's other phenomenal game?

Oh, and if I get time, I'd also like to check out Routine. It isn't exactly giving warm and cosy vibes, but I'm worried it could leave Xbox Game Pass soon, and with GTA 6 on the horizon I don't have spare funds floating around.

I've got quite a lot going on this weekend, so I don't expect to be playing too much. Hopefully I might be able to fit in some more Star Wars Galactic Racer and Tape to Tape though - both of those games are so incredible!

Voters across the country opted for nearly every local ballot measure that would curb the rate of data center expansion.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

On Tuesday, tens of millions of Americans voted in midterm elections to deliver a sweep of generational Democratic victories in federal and state races, reflecting a leftward electoral shift that's being interpreted as a nationwide rejection of Trumpism.

But even as Republican candidates and incumbents suffered defeats in what had traditionally been considered some of the party's most entrenched strongholds, the midterms also issued a stinging rebuke to another major source of voter frustration: Data centers. At nearly every opportunity, Americans voted in favor of local ballot measures to halt, slow, or stymie the pace of data center construction in their communities.

As tracked by Data Centers on the Ballot, across the 47 local midterm elections in the American cities and townships that featured ballot measures on data center construction, voters favored restrictions on the rate of data center expansion in 38 of the 39 completed counts. Of the eight races that remain open, voters supporting additional data center restrictions are leading in all six of the races with only partial reporting. For the two remaining races, no results have yet been posted.

Here's the rundown of the types of measures voters are supporting:

At time of writing, only one ballot measure that would have introduced data center restrictions failed: In Harwood, North Dakota, voters refused an amendment to the city charter that would have required Harwood to commission an independent review before approving new data center construction or expansion.

Aside from that one exception, it's not hard to suss out why so many of those measures have passed. NBC exit polls show that 56% of yesterday's midterm voters considered AI data centers either "crucial" or "a major factor" in their choice of Congress person, with data center opponents driven by concerns of environmental toll, energy costs, noise pollution, and—one must imagine—the upward-spiraling cost of RAM.

World of Warcraft: Forever, Warhammer Survivors, and a batch of fresh updates.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I can't ignore the elephant in the room: Grand Theft Auto 6 is out this month, but we still don't know when we'll see Rockstar's return trip to Vice City launch on PC. When we asked in a poll whether y'all planned to wait for the PC release, play it on console at launch, or double dip and do both, a whopping 71% said you would wait. Modding is half the fun for me, so I get it. I'm with you.

But even PC releases are dodging the big GTA 6-shaped gap in November, so what new games are even out there for you to play? Well, World of Warcraft: Forever kicks off the beginning of the month if you need a new MMO to get sucked into. Then Warhammer Survivors is just a few days later, and there's a whole slew of updates to pick through. It may be a light month, but it's not empty.

I'm eyeing a few November releases myself, though I wouldn't mind taking the time to catch up on the 2026 games I missed. As for recommendations, I'll let my colleagues take it from here.

Battle.net | November 4 World of Warcraft is 22 years old, which is bananas, and somehow I've gone all that time without touching it once. I've reported on it extensively (although not so much these days), but actually played it? Nope. With World of Warcraft: Forever coming on November 4, I'm thinking that maybe it's time to change that—to jump in and sample the greatest MMO as it was back then, but also new and improved. I'm not a GTA guy and there's not a whole hell of a lot else happening this month, so now's the time, right? Maybe. We'll see. — Andy Chalk

Steam | November 6 When this turn-based dung eon crawler first came out in 2001, it had so many technical problems our review compared it to Daikatana. One bug deleted system files when you tried to uninstall the game. 25 years later, remaster factory SNEG promises it will actually work and I can finally find out if it's any good. — Jody Macgregor

Steam | November 9 Murky water scares me to death, but I also love the rush of giddy terror, so that's why the haunted fishing excursion awaiting in Dreadmoor has my full attention. I talk a big game, but I know I'm smashing ALT+F4 the second something lunges at me from the water. Until then, I'm looking forward to its early access debut. — Andrea Shearon

Steam | November 10 I once went on a Jeep tour of Iceland. I was really hungover, but enjoyed seeing the island anyway, which says a lot, because it was a bumpy ride for someone who had recently stumbled out of a Big Lebowski-themed bar. What I'm saying is that this Euro Truck Sim 2 DLC seems like a pleasant way to get away from it all. 2— Tyler Wilde

Steam | New York's once-tranquil scenery turns into a warzone when the Echoes of Central Park expansion adds more to The Division 2 endgame.

Site | Warzone's integration into MW4 kicks off Season 1 with a player level reset, the new battle royale map: Hajin, and more.

Site | The biggest threat to Eorzea? Queue times. But worry no more as FF14 expands the duty finder pool to include all players in the same region.

Steam | The Punished DLC adds its "tortured edgelord" clan to Monster Train 2, and if PC Gamer's card-slinging expert Evan Lahti says it's a good one, then it's a good one.

Steam | The next Path of Exile expansion launches soon, but you can get an early peek when the ExileCon preview airs Friday, November 6, on Twitch.

Steam | Merchant and Republic government types usher in a new era of Crusader Kings 3 when the Silk and Silver expansion drops later in the month.

Steam | Patrol beautiful parks and kick out jerks who don't follow the rules when this sim graduates from early access.

Steam | A seaworthy update adding merfolk transformations, customizable pirate ships, and Disney adventures with the likes of Megara, Cap'n Jack Sparrow, and Dory.

Steam | Who's afraid of GTA 6? Apparently not Hooded Horse's blacksmith sim which forges its 1.0 release on the same day as Rockstar's crime sim.

Steam | There's nothing funny about the clown show happening in The Fog when The Terrifier and Sienna Shaw join DBD at the end of the month.

#4133. Rumour: Data Found In Zelda: Ocarina Of Time May Hint At Master Quest DLC

One of our main bugbears with Zelda: Ocarina of Time on Switch 2 – as incredible as it is – is that it's overall quite a breezy experience for those already familiar with the original or 3DS release.

As such, we thought it might beneficial if Nintendo were to include a more difficult mode, whether it be a simple Hero Mode in which enemies deal more damage, or perhaps even a port of the reworked Master Quest mode from the GameCube and 3DS.

Our prayers may (emphasis on the 'may') soon be answered, as a post from MrCheeze on BlueSky reveals that data found in Ocarina of Time may be hinting at some sort of Master Quest content. You'll see in the image below that many of the lines of data include 'MQ' next to the title 'DodongoCavern'.

MrCheeze has also provided more information in a follow-up post, stating "Couple strings in the exefs as well giving some context (HasMQ, IsMQModeExist, NewGameMQ, ReleaseMQ)".

So does this mean Master Quest is on the way? Potentially. We're not quite ready to put money on it, but it would certainly make sense for Nintendo to include it as part of a DLC expansion, whether free or paid.

Almost all first-party Nintendo games these days include some sort of post-launch DLC, so we've no reason to believe Ocarina of Time would be any different. As ever, though, do take all of this with a pinch of salt.

In a recent interview with IGN, producer Eiji Aonuma stated " I don't think that we would announce anything specific at this time" when asked whether Master Quest was considered for the Switch 2 remake.

Review The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time (Switch 2) - A Stunning Remake, But Not Quite Definitive

Poll What Review Score Would You Give The Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake?

"At this point what he's doing is he's inventing a new medium"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Physint star Bill Skarsgård was "very enamored" by Hideo Kojima growing up, and at this point he's far from the only Hollywood actor to feel that way.

In an appearance on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, host Josh Horowitz asks Skarsgård about his recently announced collab with Kojima, after he was announced as the lead of his upcoming Metal Gear Solid spiritual successor Physint back in September.

Skarsgård says "that's a big deal for me," and when asked if he's a gamer, he notes, "specifically the Metal Gear Solid games," adding that he "played every single" game from the PS1 title to "the last one" (presumably Metal Gear Solid 5, I can't imagine he means Survive).

He adds, "I was very enamored by him and the sort of mythology in the universes that he creates," adding, "I was really into it growing up."

Skarsgård calls Kojima an "auteur," saying "he's fluent in film making" while recalling word "way back 20 years ago" that there was talk of a Metal Gear Solid movie and the question of whether Kojima himself will direct it. Skarsgård remembers thinking, "I can't wait to see him transition it to film," but notes that "now it's gotten to the point where I asked him 'would you ever do a film?' and he's like 'no.'"

"At this point what he's doing is he's inventing a new medium," Skarsgård adds. "What we're going to do is going to be eight hours worth of narrative, right? But it's also an entire universe that you play." He calls what Kojima is doing "quite literally world building." As for Kojima himself, Skarsgård calls him a "pioneer" and says "he keeps going out into untreaded waters."

Speaking of upcoming Hideo Kojima games, Skarsgård's comments come months after OD star Hunter Schafer called the developer a "genius," with her OD co-star Sophia Lillis similarly being a fan of his games.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

This could also be our first hint of the type of game Physint is going to be, as he mentions "eight hours worth of narrative." This could be in theory a hint at the game following a format similar to the classic games in the series, with Metal Gear Solid 4 having nine hours of cutscenes. But then again, it could easily be taking the form of Metal Gear Solid 5 or Death Stranding where there's a whole lot of gameplay between those cutscenes, so maybe it's not a massive hint after all.

Hideo Kojima says Physint is "quite different" from Metal Gear: "I want plenty of new ideas and a different kind of spy action."

Scott has been freelancing for over four years across a number of different gaming publications, first appearing on GamesRadar+ in 2024. He has also written for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, VG247, Play, TechRadar, and others. He's typically rambling about Metal Gear Solid, God Hand, or any other PS2-era titles that rarely (if ever) get sequels.

#4130. Iman Vellani wants everyone to know why X-Men: The Last Stand "failed"

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Iman Vellani voices her displeasure over the third X-Men movie

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Ms. Marvel actor Iman Vellani has explained why the notorious comic book flop X-Men: The Last Stand "failed" and should have been a trilogy.

Speaking on the Countdown to Avengers: Doomsday Official Podcast that highlighted Fox's X-Men films – a key text on the road to Doomsday – Vellani first took aim at The Last Stand disposing of James Marsden's Scott Summers, before moving on to the treatment of Jean Grey and the adaptation of the Phoenix Saga storyline as a whole.

"He's integral to Jean's story in the Dark Phoenix Saga. To get rid of him in the first 10 minutes completely eliminates any emotional resonance this movie could have had," Vellani said.

If you're familiar with Vellani's Letterboxd account, you'll know she openly isn't a fan of all of Fox's X-Men movies. The Last Stand received a 2.5 score alongside X-Men 2 (ouch), with 2000's X-Men faring slightly better at 3.5.

Much of Vellani's dislike for The Last Stand is how it handles the iconic Dark Phoenix Saga arc. In Marvel's comics, Jean Grey was slowly – and tragically – transformed by the Phoenix Force, an entity that could have wiped out the entire universe. In truth, The Last Stand's abridged version didn't do it justice.

"It's so reductive of that entire storyline," Vellani said. "If they wanted to do the Phoenix Saga properly, it should have been three or four movies, even, and really milk it. There's so much that happens – it's so thrilling, cosmic, and expansive. To stuff it into one movie with 'The Cure' storyline, oh my god. This movie failed the minute they made Jean's story also secondary."

For more Phoenix Force-level hot takes, we have our own ranking of the best X-Men movies. Then, discover what else is coming to the MCU after Avengers: Doomsday with our guide to upcoming Marvel movies.

#4129. GTA 6's PS5 Physical Edition Revealed in First Photo

Images of GTA 6’s physical edition have emerged on Reddit, ahead of its release later in the month.

The anticipated open world game – which won’t include a disc – looks practically identical to every other PS5 release, in a sealed blue plastic case with the usual logos and layout.

While this is a German copy, there’s a disclaimer on the front which mentions no disc is included, and only a download code is packaged inside.

The photos, first shared on Reddit but since deleted, have been reposted below:

Fans will be able to purchase boxed versions of the Rockstar release from retailers starting 12th November, allowing a week for them to pre-load the 212GB title ahead of launch.

This is the first major title to ship in a “code-in-box” format, although it will become a lot more common in 2028, when Sony’s signalled its intent to cease manufacturing Blu-ray discs.

Personally, I’m concerned about the waste of plastic here. I understand some people may still want a case to display with their other games, but if we’re getting rid of discs, I’d like Sony to implement some sort of recyclable format moving forward.

Remember, if you want a map of Leonidas to go with your physical copy of GTA 6, you’ll need to purchase that separately for $0.99 from the Rockstar Store.

You can find out more information about GTA 6’s pre-load through here.

In the meantime, do let me know if any of you are planning to purchase the physical version and why below.

In the brief clip, which can be viewed above, we see the sky split open above what appears to be a testing site somewhere in Marion, Nevada circa 1955. At the end of the clip, we see the full title, Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Adventure, and a release window of 2028.

Joe Wright (Atonement, Pride and Prejudice) is set to direct the first three episodes, with Shawn Levy and the Duffer brothers executive-producing (H/T Variety). Because Stranger Things: The First Shadow takes place in 1959, this puts Otherworlds on a slightly earlier timeline, with the potential to go back even earlier (the same way The First Shadow has flashbacks to 1943). Plot details have yet to be revealed.

"It's Stranger Things, but also thrillingly fresh, with a new setting, new heroes and villains, and new… actually, we're not allowed to say any more. Now, on to casting. In the meantime: watch the skies, nerds," the Duffers said in a statement.

Fans initially thought that Netflix was dropping that secret ninth episode today... and this is due to the fact that the Weather Channel, the Wheel of Fortune social media accounts, and even the Duffer brothers have been teasing strange things (pun intended) all day in honor of Stranger Things Day, which is celebrated every year on November 6 as it marks that fateful day Will Byers went missing.

Other Worlds: A Stranger Things Story hits Netflix in 2028. The flagship show is available to watch in its entirety on Netflix. For more, check out our guide to the best Netflix shows, and keep up with new shows on the way.

What's leaving Xbox Game Pass in December 2026? Well, Microsoft hasn't confirmed anything just yet, but based on some games that were added to the service this time last year, we can at least make a few predictions ahead of time.

We know that a lot of Xbox users want more advance notice of games leaving Xbox Game Pass, but Microsoft usually gives us around two weeks right now - and don't forget, publishers sometimes secure late deals with Microsoft to keep their games on Game Pass, even after they've been announced to be leaving!

So, before we take a look at the following list of potential games leaving Xbox Game Pass in December 2026, we want to stress that nothing has been confirmed yet, and this will not be a 100% accurate list by any means. Some of these games might leave, some of these games might stay, and many others might be added to the list.

The most common (but definitely not the only) trend with Xbox Game Pass seems to be that games stick around for one year, so we've gone back to December 2025 to look at the games that were added to Game Pass at the time. That said, we've also gone back to the December 2024 as well, just to see what may potentially stick around for two years in total. Based on those original announcements, here's what we think could potentially leave Xbox Game Pass in December 2026:

As usual, there could be plenty of additions to this list, and a few of these games might stick around on Xbox Game Pass for even longer, but it seems likely that we'll lose at least some of these in December 2026. Our predictions usually turn out to be anywhere from 30%-80% correct - you never know how accurate they'll be!

It looks like players were right about the action RPG's storage issue

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

A minor Nier: Automata update inexplicably increased the game's Steam install size from 50GB to a stonking 366GB, and the official Nier series account has now confirmed that something's gone horribly, hilariously wrong.

"We have identified an issue following the latest update for NieR:Automata on Steam, released on November 6, 2026 (JST), where installation requires significantly more storage space than intended," a recent Twitter post from the account reads.

"We are currently investigating the cause and working to resolve the issue. We apologize for the inconvenience. As a temporary workaround, you can download the base game using the intended amount of storage space by going to 'Properties' → 'DLC' in Steam and unchecking each DLC item."

This solution aligns with player speculation that a bug with Nier: Automata's DLCs was behind the surprise hard drive gluttony. It appears that the entire 50GB game was repeatedly attached to DLC files, causing players to download it seven times. I like crossover champion 2B as much as the next Nier fan, but seven seems like too many.

At the time of writing, the Nier: Automata economy has yet to address this hyperinflation: Steam still tells us that we need 366.56GB of space to install this thing. The good news is that the game seems to be perfectly playable, assuming you can spare the space or sever those DLCs. An incredible display of video game spaghetti all around.

Nier: Automata mastermind Yoko Taro says he's still making games for "dementia prevention" and he finished his masterpiece years before Nier was even a thing

Turns out people just really want to fully own their games

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Sometimes giving Malibu Stacy a new hat works, sometimes it doesn't. Sony is learning that offering discounts and other initiatives for PlayStation users isn't enough to make people forget about the corporation stopping physical discs come 2028.

Most lucrative is the three-month free trial for YouTube Premium. Given how that platform is now an enormous part of the world of streaming, that's a decent added incentive for signing up to PlayStation's service, on top of all the games you get immediate access to.

Introducing new perks for PlayStation Plus members. Enjoy a range of special offers, trials and discounts from PlayStation, Sony and select partners. All included with your PlayStation Plus membership. Explore the full lineup: https://t.co/EuzPbZEjlw https://t.co/rXF9FtvtXpNovember 6, 2026

But none of this stacks up to what players are losing in the coming months. This year, Sony announced it would be ceasing production of discs for new games on PlayStation consoles come January 2028.

That includes PS5 and PS4. Their libraries are becoming all digital, and fans aren't happy, because such practice raises legitimate concerns over ownership. This has led to PlayStation's replies being lit up over demand for disced games.

"The only perk I want is discs," writes one fan. "Do the trials come on disc?" asks another, incredulously. "The only perk I need to enjoy is physical discs," adds a third.

Those are just the ones for this tweet. Similar replies follow every PlayStation tweet in recent weeks.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

You get the point. This has become background radiation for Sony, and I don't see it dying down any time soon. The company will have accounted for pushback, but to what degree is another question. I'm not sure I see them rolling back the decision completely, but if enough people vote with their wallets in terms of cancelling PS Plus subscriptions and getting their games elsewhere, it may force some sort of change. Physical forever.

"No disc, no buy" protest and PlayStation boycott don't bother Sony, which reports increased playtime and record-high users for September.

Theories that Bethesda is hinting at an earlier launch are already surfacing, and a few of them are pretty good.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Yesterday, after eight years of waiting, Bethesda finally gave The Elder Scrolls 6 a title: Sentinel. It then warned that, after eight years of waiting, more waiting is in store because "it'll be some time before we're ready to share more." Then Bloomberg's Jason Schreier, one of the industry's best-known and most reliable reporters, weighed in, saying the game is "still more than two years away."

Schreier's 'two more years' statement, echoed by Jez Corden of Windows Central, attracted quite a range of comments, not all of them of the polite sort. That led Schreier to Reddit, where he could elaborate on his statement.

Pointing out his record of accurate calls on previous Bethesda releases Fallout 76 and Starfield, Schreier wrote, "I'm a reporter. I am not telling you this because I enjoy watching people get mad about having to wait for sequels to their favorite video games. I am telling you this because it is true, and because my job is to report accurate facts and clear up misinformation. TES6: Sentinel is more than two years away."

Did this clarification calm the roiling waters? Well...

Many of the replies are understanding, grateful, and sympathetic to Schreier's plight, but there are plenty that express doubt or distrust, suggesting that the two year window was pure speculation. Others want to know why Bethesda would drop the title announcement yesterday if the game really is that far out, given that Todd Howard has previously expressed regret about revealing The Elder Scrolls 6 so prematurely in the first place. Why repeat that mistake?

A few optimistic souls are holding onto the dream of a 2027 release that emerged from the reveal trailer for Skyrim on the Nintendo Switch 2:

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

And then there are the Elder Scrolls fans operating on a whole different level from the rest of us. Redditor Reacryoum, for instance, thinks Bethesda is leading up to a surprise trailer drop on November 11—that's actually one of the more grounded theories to emerge over the past 24 hours. Casting back to one of Bethesda's old Twitter posts, Jayehemcee speculated that the theme of the game is "time," and that this is all part of the game's marketing. I'm not sure how that one works in practice, frankly, but I respect the ambition.

Minimum-Act-7571 put forth the idea that Bethesda is actually messing with Schreier by intentionally feeding him false information, because it's super mad at him spilling the beans all the time—although they also admitted that it's a "new copium theory," and so perhaps not meant to be taken entirely seriously.

I think the best of the bunch, though, is this one from Any-West7160, who believes the Sentinel title reveal contains the actual release date: November 11, 2027. I don't believe it, but I like it.

Here's the video in question—what do you see in the stars?

The best videogame conspiracy theories are always the most bonkers, but what complicates the situation just a wee little bit for Sentinel is that one such theory was actually correct: The Sentinel subtitle was stashed away in a Starfield easter egg for years before anyone noticed. Maybe it was just a coincidence, sure, but the numbers don't lie, as the saying goes—and those numbers said Sentinel. And they were right!

So there's precedent there, pretty certainly, but it's also a lot easier to drop in a reference to a locked-in-stone game title than it is to do the same with a relatively far-off launch date that's subject to disruption and delays. And as others have pointed out, including Schreier, it's extremely unlikely that anyone is just lying about the far-off release window for a little bit of PR pop: Evasion and word games are one thing, but straight-up dishonesty will leave your credibility in shreds pretty much instantly.

What it all adds up to, ultimately, is this: Two more years of waiting and maybe more, plenty of hopium and copium along the way, and a wise piece of advice from Vanquisher_84 which will almost certainly go unheeded:

For a period of the PS5 generation, Sony ported its games to the PC, rendering very few of its titles genuine exclusives.

In the last year and a bit it’s made an internal decision to focus solely on exclusivity, and it’s slowly beginning to promote that again.

As spotted by power user Radec on social media, the official PlayStation.com pages for Ghost of Yotei and Until Dawn 2 now include ‘PlayStation Exclusive’ logos.

While the manufacturer experimented with bringing its first-party titles to Steam, sales were allegedly poor.

This proves the company is now doubling down on exclusivity again, although it has said it’ll continue to release select multiplayer and live service games on PC, such as this year’s Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls.

I imagine we’re going to see Sony start to tout the ‘PlayStation Exclusive’ branding more aggressively once it rebuilds its library, beginning with next year’s God of War Laufey and (hopefully) Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet.
